My families spaghetti sauce recipe

1 large can diced tomato

1 large can crushed tomatos

1 regular can sliced stewed tomato

1 small can tomato paste

3-5 garlic cloves minced

1/2 large yellow onion diced

2 celery stalks diced

2 carrots grated

3 tbsp basil

5 tbsp parsley

2 tsp oregano

Piuch of red pepper flakes

1 bay leaf

Start your sauce pot on low. Add olive oil and a pat of butter. Let that heat up

Add the onions, celery, carrots, a fee pinches of salt, pepper and half the basil.

Let that cook very low, no sizzling for 15-20 minutes until onions are translucent.

Next add garlic, bay leaf and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Cook another 5-10 minutes until garlic is soft.

Add all the can tomatos now, the rest of the spices. A pinch of sugar to help get rid of the tinny taste from the can tomatos. You can also add beef or chicken stock if you would like at this point.

Simmer on low from 2 hours to the whole day if you have time.

Bonus leftovers can be turned into chili if you add cooked ground beef, beans, chili powder paprika and a dash of cumin

I got a recipe that I always use when I want to impress people. It worked on my wife before we were dating. Its on the grill but you could probably cook it in the oven and then add a little liquid smoke to the vinegar sauce at end and get similar results.

North Carolina Pulled Pork

  • 1 pork shoulder, 5-6 lbs
  • 1 tbsp mild paprika
  • 2 tsp light brown sugar
  • 1.25 tsp hot paprika (can sub with half mild paprika and half cayenne pepper)
  • .5 tsp celery salt
  • .5 tsp garlic salt
  • .5 tsp dry mustard
  • .5 tsp ground black pepper
  • .5 tsp onion powder
  • .5 tsp salt

Steps

  1. Combine dry ingredients in a bowl and mix to a uniform blend. Rub the mixture all over the pork shoulder. Then wrap the shoulder in plastic wrap and chill for 2-8 hours or overnight.
  2. Setup the grill for indirect heat with a temp of 300 F
  3. Place the should on the grill, fat side up. Add wood chips, if desired. Cover the grill and cook the shoulder until the internal temp is 195 F, approximately 4-6 hours.
  4. Carefully transfer the shoulder to a cutting board, it should be fall-off-the bone-tender. Allow the shoulder to rest for 15 minutes under a foil tent.
  5. Pull the pork apart with forks or your hands until the whole shoulder is shredded. This can take up to 20 minutes or longer.
  6. Transfer pork to a mixing bowl and add in 1-1.5 cup of Vinegar Sauce(recipe below).
  7. Serve on a hamburger bun with pickles and sliced onion or with cole slaw.

Vinegar Sauce

  • 2 c cider vinegar(I use apple)
  • .5 c + 2 tbsp ketchup
  • .25 c packed brown sugar
  • 5 tsp salt
  • 4 tsp hot red pepper flakes
  • 1 tsp ground black pepper
  • 1 tsp ground white pepper
  • 1.5 c water

Combine ingredients in a bowl and whisk until sugar, salt, and ketchup disolve.
